meta.title: Product Engineer | Tano Careers | Tano
meta.description: Product Engineer at Tano, in person in central London: own the agent that runs influencer marketing end-to-end, in production, for paying brands.

blocks.html: You would own the influencer affiliate management agent: the system that turns a single successful post into a months-long relationship, and a one-off affiliate into a real brand ambassador. It is our hardest, highest-leverage surface, because it runs unattended over months with no human left to babysit it. You own the design, the build, the ship and the architecture, and as the team grows it becomes the foundation others build on.
If you want to point at a system in production and say you designed it, this is the closest seat there is to being a technical founder.

items: You ship across the whole stack, backend and frontend, without waiting to be told what to build.
You have built and shipped real AI agents or application-layer AI in production (not demos or prompt wrappers), and you know where these systems break.
Product taste: you make good calls on scope and UX without a PM.
At your best in ambiguity, on a team that ships continuously.
Roughly 5 to 7 years in, and ideally someone who wants to be a technical founder themselves within a few years.
Bonus: Go · LangGraph or comparable agent frameworks · Postgres and Supabase depth · zero-to-one experience · a feel for the creator economy.

blocks.html: TypeScript (NestJS, Next.js) and Go, with Postgres, LangGraph, Google Gemini, Supabase, Fly.io and Vercel. Early enough that you will shape it.

items.body: Fastest-promoted engineer at a London YC scale-up.

blocks.html: Alongside a tight team across influencer and customer ops who do, by hand, the work the agents are learning to do. We own the outcomes, so we know exactly what a working agent has to be.
Whoever has the context decides, by writing it down and shipping it, not by waiting for a meeting. We ship to live brands continuously and let real usage tell us what is true.

items.title: Two 30-minute calls with Sagar and Will: motivation and technical depth.
Onsite, mostly with Sagar: a system design task and sometimes a product build, plus time with the team and lunch.

blocks.html: Roughly two weeks end to end.

rows: Health insurance, onsite gym, in-person culture, real startup work-life

blocks.html: Tell us why you, and what you'd want to own. We read every application.
